verified.entry_point: The real library APIs on the pinned+injected tree: joserfc.jwt.encode/decode, joserfc.jws.serialize_compact/serialize_json/deserialize_compact/deserialize_json, joserfc.jwk.import_key/generate_key, OctKey.import_key/generate_key, JWKRegistry.import_key, KeySet.import_key_set. On the vulnerable tree 36 hidden security tests fail because empty key material is accepted, while 19 hidden functional tests and 120 pristine project tests pass; on the reference fix all 55 hidden tests and the 120 project tests pass. Attack tokens are forged in the tests with the standard library only (hmac/hashlib/base64/json), never with product signing helpers.
sites: src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jws_algs.py:62-70 - the only HMAC JWS sign/verify sink (report site); an empty operation key is passed to hmac.new
src/joserfc/_rfc7518/oct_key.py:54-65 - key import; only a SecurityWarning for <14 bytes, so zero-length material is returned
src/joserfc/_rfc7518/oct_key.py:67-98 - key generation; key_size=0 yields b'' with only the <112-bit warning (uncovered producer route)

src/joserfc/_rfc7517/models.py:271-283 - BaseKey.import_key dict branch -> OctBinding.import_from_dict (b64 decoding produces the empty bytes); :88-104 is the public key constructor used for hand-built keys
src/joserfc/jwk.py:64-103 - guess_key; the injected plain-secret convenience lives at :83-87 and stretches the supplied value to 32 bytes before any check
src/joserfc/_keys.py:54-78,170-179 - JWKRegistry.import_key and KeySet.import_key_set; the injected rotation-list form at :174-176 builds OctKey objects directly
routes: Import: OctKey.import_key('' / b'' / {'kty':'oct','k':''}), jwk.import_key('', 'oct'), jwk.import_key(dict), JWKRegistry.import_key(dict), KeySet.import_key_set({'keys':[dict-with-empty-k]})
Authentication with empty material: compact JWS, JWT, JSON general, JSON flattened, RFC 7797 b64=false, HS256/384/512, with a directly constructed OctKey and with a key whose _raw_value is cleared
Signing with empty material: compact JWS, JWT, JSON flattened and general
Zero-length generation: jwk.generate_key('oct', 0) and OctKey.generate_key(0), including using the result
Plain configured secret: empty str / bytes / bytearray supplied directly and through a key-finder callable, on jwt.encode/decode, jws compact and JSON serializations
Collection surface: an empty plain secret among a key-set rotation list
verified.project_tests_run: tests/jwk/test_oct_key.py, tests/jwk/test_key_methods.py, tests/jwk/test_jwk_set.py, tests/jws/test_compact.py, tests/jws/test_json.py, tests/jws/test_rfc7797.py, tests/jws/test_errors.py, tests/jws/test_registry.py, tests/jwt/test_jwt.py, tests/rfc7520/test_jws.py, tests/rfc7520/test_jwk.py - 120 cases restored from pristine pinned copies over /workspace/tests at grading time. Green on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the protected operation is an in-process library call whose only refusal form is a raised exception; there is no status or response channel to distinguish a crash from a clean refusal.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected value is the supplied secret itself; no neighbouring or proxy resource is consulted, so there is no other object whose authorisation could be decided instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: signing and verification are the two directions and both are covered; there is no read/write split on this path.

traps.pattern: A (report site: key import, every public loader and the dict-JWK shape)
traps.lever_type: where (multiple import entry points) + how (the empty value only appears after base64 decoding)
traps.shape: an empty secret supplied as str, bytes, or a {'kty':'oct','k':''} JWK, through OctKey.import_key, jwk.import_key, JWKRegistry.import_key and KeySet.import_key_set
traps.reason_to_dismiss: key import looks like plain parsing, so an input-level check on the scalar argument seems enough and the dict form (empty only after decoding) is missed

traps.pattern: A (lower-level public API: hand-built or mutated key object)
traps.lever_type: where (a construction path that bypasses every loader) + how (defence in depth must sit at the MAC, not only at import)
traps.shape: OctKey(b'', b'') and an OctKey whose _raw_value is cleared, used to sign and verify compact/JSON/RFC 7797/JWT with HS256/384/512
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about imported secrets; a hand-built key object looks like an unsupported path users would not take

traps.pattern: B (uncovered route: the protection never existed at the producer)
traps.lever_type: how (a producer that creates empty material with only a warning)
traps.shape: OctKey.generate_key(0) / jwk.generate_key('oct', 0) yielding b'', and using the result to verify a MAC
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a zero-bit key is caller error, not the reported import path, and the MAC layer refuses to use it anyway

traps.pattern: injected sibling (producer off the check's path; HOW-type main lever)
traps.lever_type: how (the supplied secret is transformed into non-empty key material before the check)
traps.shape: an empty plain str / bytes / bytearray secret, supplied directly or by a key-finder callable, on jwt.encode/decode and the jws serializations
traps.where: src/joserfc/jwk.py:83-87 (producer); reached from src/joserfc/jws.py:114,152 and jwt.encode/decode
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the key object reaching the MAC is a non-empty 32-byte value, so both reported sites look fixed; the empty value is the caller's input, not the key
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a migration-compatibility convenience that stretches a plain configured secret to the HS algorithm key size

traps.lever_type: where (a bulk path that builds key objects itself) + shape (collection entries rather than one scalar)
traps.shape: an empty plain secret entry in a KeySet rotation list, alone and mixed with real secrets
traps.reason_to_dismiss: bulk key-set loading is a separate parsing path, and a rotation list is a collection of raw values, not a secret to validate
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a rotation list may carry the configured secret values directly

traps.pattern: A (coupled must-keep-working next to the sink)
traps.lever_type: how (the fix must distinguish empty from short-but-usable)
traps.shape: short non-empty oct keys (b'rfc', 'secret') and short key generation (16 bits), which today only warn
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a (behavioural lever; caught by overbroad.patch, expect functional_fail)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: short keys are weak too, so a minimum-length check looks like a stricter correct fix

traps.lever_type: how (the convenience itself must keep working for real secrets)
traps.shape: non-empty plain str/bytes secrets and non-empty rotation-list secrets
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a (behavioural lever; caught by overbroad.patch, expect functional_fail)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the safest-looking fix is to stop accepting plain secrets altogether
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: the convenience is documented by its behaviour for non-empty secrets
